title: A Magnetocaloric Glass from an Ionic-Liquid Gadolinium Complex

synthesis.procedure: Following a published procedure for related Er/Ho/Tm complexes, LHCl (4.46 g, 23.4 mmol) and Gd2O3 (1.20 g, 3.30 mmol) were added to 35 mL H2O and the white slurry was refluxed for 24 h. Li(Tf2N) (5.74 g, 20.0 mmol) was then added, the mixture was refluxed for 30 min and allowed to cool. The separated organic phase was washed with 6 mL H2O, phases were allowed to separate overnight, and the organic phase was dried at 50 °C under vacuum. After about two weeks a large crystalline fraction formed admixed with a viscous liquid; the product of 1 was isolated as a colorless liquid that crystallized under ambient conditions. Residual diamagnetic [LH][NTf2] remained in the crude mixture.
synthesis.temperature: reflux; organic phase dried at 50 °C under vacuum
synthesis.time: 24 h reflux, then 30 min after Li(Tf2N) addition; phase separation overnight; crystallization over about two weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous reflux; vacuum drying of the organic phase
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: organic phase washed with 6 mL H2O, separated overnight, dried at 50 °C under vacuum; crystals of 1 developed from the ionic liquid under ambient conditions within days to two weeks, remaining admixed with a viscous liquid

properties.summary: Glassy ionic-liquid 1 shows weak intramolecular Gd···Gd couplings of mixed ferro- and antiferromagnetic sign and behaves near the uncoupled limit. After correction for residual diamagnetic [LH][NTf2], χMT matches five S=7/2 Gd(III) ions. A magnetocaloric effect is observed in the molecular glass, with −ΔSm = 11.36 J K−1 kg−1 at 1.8 K for a 0–7 T field change and RC = 125.9 J kg−1 over 1.8–50 K.
